query: What signals suggest a goal will be highly achieved?

per_column.name: achievement_score
per_column.rationale: A continuous achievement measure is essentially the underlying quantity from which high_goal_achievement is derived; it restates/leaks the outcome rather than predicting it.

per_column.name: status_is_completed
per_column.rationale: Whether the goal is completed is only knowable at/after the outcome and is nearly deterministic with achievement, constituting post-outcome leakage rather than a predictive signal.

per_column.name: priority_is_high
per_column.rationale: A binary flag derived from priority is a legitimate ex-ante attribute that lies outside the focus and could plausibly correlate with achievement without restating it.

per_column.name: completion_rate_high
per_column.rationale: This is a thresholded version of percent_complete, which is essentially the same construct as goal achievement; it is a deterministic restatement/leak of the focus.

per_column.name: time_spent_ratio
per_column.rationale: Elapsed-time-over-total ratio is only fully known once the goal period concludes and correlates with completion progress; as computed here it reflects outcome-time information (leakage) rather than a clean ex-ante predictor.

judge.rationale: The set is dominated by restatements and post-outcome measures of achievement/completion (achievement_score, status_is_completed, completion_rate_high, time_spent_ratio), which leak the focus rather than predict it. Only priority_is_high is a genuine ex-ante predictor, and it is a single weak binarized feature, so the set provides little legitimate predictive leverage beyond the original columns.
